title_line: Operations Leader  |  Warehouse, Quality & Fulfillment  |  PMP
summary: Operations leader who has run warehouse returns, quality, inventory, and overseas manufacturing for a consumer products company, and built the SOPs and metrics that make that work repeatable. At Lion Energy, Eric cut return-to-resolution time about 50% across roughly 10,000 partner returns a year, brought root cause investigations down from months to about a week, and contributed to an estimated $100,000 in first-year savings on processing, storage, and labor. He has grown teams, trained reps and partners, owned a team budget, and helped products move from prototype into production. A PMP and Certified Scrum Product Owner with eight years in Vivint's sales organization, he wants to help a growing consumer brand scale its operations without losing the quality customers buy it for.
skills: Quality control and root cause analysis

roles.title: Product Owner (promoted from Project Manager)
roles.scope: Worked across the warehouse, QA, engineering, and manufacturing partners in China and Vietnam for a consumer portable power and solar products company, from product development through returns.
bullets: Improved the return-to-resolution workflow by about 50% in a partner-return operation handling roughly 10,000 returns a year.
Reduced yearly RMAs by 10%, and helped reduce partner product returns by 15% over several months.
Cut root cause investigation time from months to about one week.
Contributed to an estimated $100,000 in first-year savings on return processing, storage, and labor.
Wrote clearer receiving, inspection, and documentation procedures for returned products and improved barcode-based return tracking.
Got warehouse staff, engineering, QA, and manufacturing suppliers working from the same defect data, and coordinated corrective action on recurring hinge, wiring, and frame defects.
Moved the PPG2500 portable power station into production and took the Peak line and Safari cart through prototype, balancing cost, weight, packaging, and manufacturing constraints.
Coordinated packaging drop-test, FCC, and UL certification activities.
Introduced Agile and Scrum and wrote a technology department handbook covering project management, QA, rollback, and launch procedures.

roles.title: Project Manager (Independent Contractor)
roles.scope: Ran residential construction jobs from start to finish across Utah and Salt Lake counties and built the operating systems behind them.
bullets: Put construction management SOPs in place.
Added inventory tracking and an equipment maintenance program.
Managed the vehicle fleet.
Set up quality and safety controls on job sites.

roles.title: Inside Sales Representative
roles.scope: Sells smart-home and energy-management systems in Vivint's national inside sales group.
bullets: Converts 30% of outbound leads and keeps sales-to-install completion above 90%.
Leads a 70% attachment rate on Vivint's Smart Comfort energy-management program.

roles.title: Product Owner (promoted from Project Manager)
roles.scope: Owned operational software and technology projects for a national services company, working with operations, finance, sales, legal, and executive leadership.
bullets: Coordinated a major data and technology migration that contributed to an estimated $3 million or more in annual recurring savings by reducing vendor dependence.
Contributed to estimated annual savings of about $250,000 on rent overpayments and $375,000 on vacancy and placement management.
Product Owner for software used by more than 2,000 seasonal reps; coordinated about 12 developers, including overseas contributors.
Contributed to a reported 29% relative drop in onboarding dropout from a baseline of about 25%.

roles.title: Area Manager, Post-Sale Operations
roles.location: Las Vegas and Arizona markets (based in Orem, UT)
bullets: Contributed to a 57% increase in PTO processing rate by improving project tracking and clearing bottlenecks between departments.

roles.title: Junior Project Manager
bullets: Kept the warehouse and inventory organized and ordered job materials to match project schedules.
Scheduled rotating crews and coordinated up to ten contractors on remodeling jobs from handoff to completion.

roles.title: Analytics Manager (four progressive roles)
roles.scope: Moved from inside sales to account manager, analytics manager, and enterprise partner sales and training over eight years.
bullets: Helped build an installation-support department from more than 20 reps to more than 50.
Coordinated a four-person analytics team that built sales and installation dashboards and commission tracking tools, supporting a reported 34% relative improvement in sales-to-install conversion.
Designed and delivered training for hundreds of independent sales partners, contributing to more than $1 million in new annual revenue.

earlier: Lead Home Manager, Lindon Care and Training (2009–2011): ran daily operations of a residential care facility, including staffing, schedules, training, safety procedures, and incident documentation.
Fabrication Worker, AA Machine and Welding (2007–2009): industrial fabrication and shop-floor production. Concrete Foreman, Paramount Homes (2004–2006): supervised ground crews and equipment.
education: Bachelor of Business Administration (Business Management), Utah Valley University
Project Management Professional (PMP), Project Management Institute, 2021

paragraphs: Growing brands usually feel it first in the warehouse. Returns pile up, nobody knows why a product keeps failing, and customer service ends up absorbing the cost. Fixing that kind of problem is the work I've done best.

At Lion Energy I worked between our warehouse, engineering team, and manufacturers in China and Vietnam. We were handling about 10,000 partner returns a year, and a single root cause investigation could take months. I wrote clearer receiving and inspection procedures, tightened up barcode tracking, and got everyone looking at the same defect data. Investigations dropped to about a week. Resolution time fell roughly 50%, yearly RMAs fell 10%, and we estimated $100,000 in first year savings. Before that, I helped grow a Vivint support team from about 20 people to more than 50, then designed training for hundreds of sales partners.

But what draws me to Manly Bands is the mix. Warehouse, manufacturing, quality, and customer support under one leader is how I like to work, because the fixes usually live in the handoffs between them. I'm a PMP, I've owned a team budget, and I'm ready to help you scale without slowing down the people making the rings. Can we find time next week to talk?
